title: About
description: About Blue Shark Friends and the co-founders, Hannah Parker and Josie Stewart. A company run by two disabled trans women to serve the transgender community. BIPOC led, Black led
about_bsf:
Blue Shark Friends is a worker-owned digital community building company. We started as a software development company that in many ways was part of the post-pandemic small business boom, but our story is rooted in more than just a reaction to the evolving economic pressures at large.

Our commitment to making software for trans people was drawn from our experiences as disabled trans people fighting to survive the current cissexist regime.

We feel that the key to surviving these times is to strengthen the bonds within our community. We want to be more than a business—we want to build a network of trans enterprises that reflects and reinforces our chosen family.

Now, in our third year of business, we have grown our community, both within and beyond the boundaries of our business. We are a community of artists and tech professionals, and we want to share our resources with your communities. We're building tools, we're building practices, and we're creating the beauty we want to see in the world. If you're interested, we invite you to get to know us a little better, as we figure out how to build digital community in a more sustainable way.

people.name: Hannah Parker
people.title: Community Weaver
people.bio: Hi!  I am a Community Weaver for Blue Shark Friends.  I build relationships.  Within our community.  With partners.  With friends.  With you.
people.img_alt: Picture of Hannah - a black trans woman crouching on a concrete porch and leaning against a green colored wall of house.  She has long black hair, a teal shirt with a picture of a wolf and is smiling.  She is proudly holding a cane in her right hand.

people.name: Josie Stewart
people.title: Engineering Strategist
people.bio:
After working for over a decade as a professional software engineer, I was pushed out of my corporate job after asking for accommodations. I knew I needed to be doing something for my people. I've been embedded in tech development since early childhood, and I wanted to find a way to use my skillset within my community. As a disabled trans woman, sometimes it feels like I have to tell my whole life story for anything about me to make sense. But in the age of Flock cameras and paid Nazi agitators on social media, I don't think you need to know my story to know why we're here.

Blue Shark Friends is important to me, first and foremost, because I need it. I believe community-built and community-supported technology is the only way forward. Not just for me, but for us all.

A lot of folks have already turned to self-employment, and technology is an unavoidable lifeline. I know we can help folks out with our background, and I believe we have to. We need to be a true community—directing our energies and skills into each other as much as possible.
people.img_alt: Picture of Josie - a smiling blue-haired trans woman with purple-rimmed glasses standing in front of a brick wall

people.name: Juniper Lusby
people.title: Art Director
people.bio: Existing at the intersection of queer and disabled and divorced from familial support, I have had to absolutely claw my way out of the gutter and Blue Shark Friends has been instrumental in finding my footing. All I really want is to get my head above water and help others do the same.

people.title: Marketing Strategist
people.bio: I'm a disabled parent of cats trying to create space for my family and yours.
